engagement_background.objective: Generate $240K–$470K in cost savings through a six-month strategic sourcing program that leverages Savida Health’s enterprise purchasing power while maintaining or improving service levels and product quality.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Approximately $5.3 million in baseline indirect spend across 10 categories (EMR, employee benefits, lab & medical supplies, IT hardware, telecom, office supplies, small parcel, commercial print, waste management). About 85-90 % of this spend is considered addressable; lower-value categories may be dropped if savings potential is minimal.
constraints_challenges: Supplier non-responsiveness to data requests, causing potential delays in baselining and RFP preparation.
Incumbent supplier sensitivities and pushback, requiring a unified Savida/Treya negotiating front.
Risk of unsanctioned “side conversations” with suppliers that could undermine sourcing strategy.
Limited stakeholder availability for data provision, interviews, and timely feedback.
Aggressive timeline to secure quick-hit savings by year-end 2024 and complete all sourcing waves by mid-March 2025.
Incomplete internal usage data—Treya must obtain line-item history from high-spend suppliers to build representative baselines.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Basic AP/PO data and current contracts exist, but detailed line-item usage often resides with suppliers; Treya must request additional data to create spend baselines.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: No centralized contract repository; usage data gaps and inconsistent formats require supplier outreach and data cleansing.
